answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying power to a verifiable work history rather than to account creation. Every new identity starts with narrow limits, and its reputation grows only as peers attest completed tasks over a long horizon, recorded in a public atlas of past work. An attacker who spawns thousands of clones must repeat that costly history for each one, while a genuine agent climbs gradually toward its zenith of trust. Faking scale therefore costs real work, not just new names.
